appraisal_events.evidence: « celle que j'avais aimée n'était plus, au bout d'un certain temps, qu'un pâle souvenir » ; « il n'y aurait pas plus de traces de mon amour pour Albertine qu'il n'y en avait eu [...] de mon amour pour ma grand'mère » ; le nouveau moi « croyait la connaître, elle lui était sympathique, il l'aimait, mais ce n'était qu'une tendresse de seconde main ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage is organized around the completion of forgetting: Albertine loses every claim on the narrator, surviving only as a pale memory and a second-hand tenderness felt by a self that never knew her. The narrator explicitly endorses this reduction as an accomplished fact rather than merely reporting it.

appraisal_events.evidence: « la fatigue et la tristesse que je ressentais » ; se plaire « avec de nouveaux vivants, de purs gens du monde, de simples amis des Guermantes, si peu intéressants par eux-mêmes » ; « notre sénilité bavarde, mélancolique et coquette » ; une vie « si dépourvu[e] du support d'un moi individuel identique et permanent [...] si inutile dans l'avenir » — bien que l'oubli apporte « une suppression presque complète de la souffrance, une possibilité de bien-être ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator turns the analysis on himself and lowers his own standing: the relief he gains is the work of a substitute self, and he ironizes his new contentment with insignificant society acquaintances as chattering senility, framing his life as a discontinuous, unsupported, futile succession.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine loses all remaining hold over the narrator: the self that could suffer for her has been replaced, and what love remains for her is explicitly second-hand.
She is locally devalued not by blame but by dissolution: reduced to a pale memory of the same order as the forgotten grandmother, an object of pity-free retrospection.
The narrator diminishes himself, treating his new sociability with uninteresting Guermantes hangers-on as parasitic vegetation and garrulous senility.
The suppression of suffering is real but is purchased by the substitution of a new self; the passage's governing affects remain fatigue, sadness, and the loss of a permanent identity.

ambiguities: The narrator's own movement is genuinely double-signed: the new « moi » is called « si bienfaisant » and brings « une possibilité de bien-être », which could support a positive emotional_position reading, but the passage's dominant framing (fatigue, sadness, the death of the former self, life as a futile succession) makes the diminishment reading the stronger one; this is deliberate relief rather than narrator-endorsed renewal.
